issues.passage: The team treated the salient findings as minor footnotes unlikely to affect the conclusion.
issues.why: “Salient findings” is correct use (most noticeable/important). The team’s poor treatment does not make the word misuse; a careful reader would accept the sentence as coherent English.

fix.correctPassage: Among several results, the most salient was the unexpected rise in retention rates.
wrongPassages: Editors wanted a salient claim that would blend into the appendix and escape every reviewer’s notice.
She reserved the label salient for a tiny typo while insisting the fatal sampling error barely mattered.
His salient contribution was so slight that colleagues forgot he had joined the project.

issues.passage: She ranked a small typo as the report’s most salient flaw and set aside the sampling error.
issues.why: Ranking something as the “most salient flaw” is natural, correct use of salient = most noticeable or important. Poor prioritization is not word misuse; the sentence is valid English.

issues.passage: The new route will thwart delivery delays by adding direct service between the two hubs.
issues.why: “Thwart delivery delays” is a valid, natural use of thwart = prevent (delays from occurring). Adding direct service is a plausible way to prevent delays, so the sentence is correct English.

fix.correctPassage: Strict export rules may thwart researchers’ efforts to share the dataset internationally.
wrongPassages: The grant was designed to thwart the study by covering equipment, travel, and staff time.
Early feedback helped thwart the proposal by clarifying weak sections before submission.
The new route will thwart on-time deliveries by adding direct service between the two hubs.
